sentences.text: El Niño is the periodic appearance of unusually warm water off the coast of Peru in the eastern Pacific, accompanied by large-scale changes in atmospheric circulation.
During El Niño, warm water from the central Pacific drifts eastwards and temporarily replaces the cold Peruvian (Humboldt) Current.
The name, meaning 'the Christ Child', comes from its appearance around Christmas.
The warming reduces plankton and hence the fish catch off Peru.
El Niño is linked to the Southern Oscillation, a see-saw in surface pressure measured between Tahiti and Darwin.
The combined phenomenon is called ENSO.
In strong ENSO years the arid west coast of South America receives heavy rain, while Australia and sometimes India suffer drought.
El Niño is therefore used in India for long-range monsoon forecasting.
However, a positive Indian Ocean Dipole can offset part of its adverse effect.
Since ENSO events recur irregularly, India needs better ocean monitoring and drought-proofed, contingency-ready agriculture.
